question: An investigator is attempting to develop a blood test to diagnose sporadic Creutzfeld-Jacob disease (CJD). She has collected several tissue samples from adults who were diagnosed with CJD. After performing a comprehensive tissue analysis, she has identified two amino acid sequences on the affected proteins that are highly consistent across samples. She then creates antibodies that are highly specific to those amino acid sequences and is interested in using those antibodies to identify similar sequences in individuals suspected of having CJD. Which of the following tests would be most helpful in identifying these individuals?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Antibodies specific to amino acid sequences -> Bind to similar sequences in individuals suspected of having CJD -> Identify affected individuals -> 80% CHAIN: Western blot -> Utilizes antibodies specific to amino acid sequences -> Detects proteins with similar sequences in suspected CJD individuals -> Helpful in diagnosing CJD -> 80%
enhanced_information: The most helpful test in identifying individuals suspected of having sporadic Creutzfeld-Jacob disease (CJD) would be the Western blot. This test utilizes antibodies specific to the identified amino acid sequences on affected proteins to detect proteins with similar sequences in suspected CJD individuals, aiding in the diagnosis of CJD. The evidence paths linking antibodies to symptoms and disease predisposition in Creutzfeldt-Jakob Syndrome do not directly support the diagnostic utility of Western blot but highlight the role of antibodies in disease processes.
analysis: The core medical principle here is utilizing antibodies specific to identified amino acid sequences on affected proteins to aid in the diagnosis of sporadic Creutzfeld-Jacob disease (CJD). The Western blot test is the most appropriate choice as it allows for the detection of proteins with similar sequences in suspected CJD individuals using these specific antibodies.
